$comment: The frozen project graph. ADR 0001 prints this table; rule A7 asserts multiset equality
between the resolved checkout and this file, so an edge added without amending ADR 0001
fails, and so does an edge the ADR promises that the checkout no longer has.
Generated at VM-0 and hand-maintained thereafter; the docs test asserting that the
printed table matches this file is deferred to VM-6.
VM-1 adds the two test-only projects ADR 0001's budget permits - the composition-root host
and the behavioural contract suite - taking the graph from 5 projects and 8 edges to 7 and
16. It adds ZERO packable assemblies: the packable set stays exactly the three product
packages, and a fourth PackageId before VM-3 requires a dated revision of ADR 0001.

VM-2 adds the one test-only project ADR 0001's budget permits it - a fuzz target host - taking the graph from 7 projects and 16 edges to 8 and 20. That is the ceiling the record names: 5 test-only projects and 8 in total. It adds ZERO packable assemblies, so the packable set is still exactly the three product packages.

VM-3 adds the four projects ADR 0001 revision 1 authorises - two application-local consumer profiles and two named composition roots - taking the graph from 8 projects and 20 edges to 12 and 33, and test-only projects from 5 to 7. It adds ZERO packable assemblies: the packable set is still exactly the three product packages. The composition roots are the only projects permitted to reference a profile assembly, which is the deployment boundary src/compositions/ exists to enforce.

VM-4 adds the one test-only project ADR 0001 revision 2 authorises - a soak host whose managed heap and working set are sampled over a long lifecycle run - taking the graph from 12 projects and 33 edges to 13 and 37, and test-only projects from 7 to 8. It adds ZERO packable assemblies, so the packable set is still exactly the three product packages.

VM-5 adds the one test-only project ADR 0001 revision 3 authorises - an uninstrumented benchmark host that publishes what the core costs a profile - taking the graph from 13 projects and 37 edges to 14 and 41, and test-only projects from 8 to 9. It adds ZERO packable assemblies, so the packable set is still exactly the three product packages. It references no benchmarking package: a framework's own warmup, pilot and outlier policies would be part of every figure the component publishes and none of them would be visible in this repository.

JS-0 adds the three project shells the JavaScript profile's own ADR-equivalent decision JSD-0001 authorises - the format assembly, the profile assembly and the lowering - taking the graph from 14 projects and 41 edges to 17 and 46, and product projects from 3 to 6. It adds ZERO packable assemblies: all three declare IsPackable false and no PackageId, so the packable set is still exactly the three core packages and rule A6 still counts three. The profile assembly references Abstractions, Binary and its own format sibling, which ADR 0011 P1's 2026-08-31 revision admits; the lowering references Abstractions and the format and never the profile, which is what makes an execution-only composition compiler-free. ADR 0001 revision 5 authorises the growth.

JS-1 adds the two composition roots ADR 0001 revision 6 authorises - an execution-only root and a slice-compiler root - taking the graph from 17 projects and 46 edges to 19 and 55. It adds ZERO packable assemblies. The two are separate projects rather than two modes of one because their REFERENCE SETS differ by the lowering, which is the whole of the execution-only claim: that root names the profile and not the compiler, so it cannot turn source into an artifact however it is invoked, and every artifact it runs is precompiled and read as bytes.

JS-3a adds the conformance harness, which ADR 0001's revision of 2026-09-03 authorises: a composition root that is NEVER ADVERTISED, taking the graph from 20 projects and 59 edges to 21 and 64. It adds ZERO packable assemblies. Its reference set is the slice-compiler root's, because scoring a conformance test means lowering it - and rule N13 is what holds the consequence: the harness, and any suite it reads, appear in no package and in no advertised composition's closure, and no other project references it in either direction.

JS-3b adds ONE composition root and it is the first here to claim a deployment label: the end-user host, which ADR 0001 revision of 2026-09-03 authorises. It takes the graph from 21 projects and 64 edges to 22 and 69, and adds ZERO packable assemblies. Its reference set is the conformance root's and the slice-compiler root's - the profile plus the lowering - so it introduces no new edge SHAPE; what it introduces is a composition that is handed SOURCE FROM OUTSIDE THE IMAGE, which is the one thing `narrow-runtime-compiler` means that a root lowering a programmatic builder cannot demonstrate. It is the only JavaScript root carrying no test tooling at all, which is what makes its closure readable against the label rather than needing the paragraph of exceptions every sibling needs.

WA-0 adds the three projects the WebAssembly profile's boundary milestone needs - the profile assembly, an execution-only composition root and a never-advertised harness root - taking the graph from 22 projects and 69 edges to 25 and 79. It adds ZERO packable assemblies: the profile declares IsPackable false and no PackageId, and neither root is advertised, so the packable set is still exactly the three core packages. The profile assembly references Abstractions and Binary and NOTHING ELSE: unlike the JavaScript profile it has no format sibling, because its payload is a bare WebAssembly module produced by an external toolchain and there is no lowering for a pivot to hold apart. The two roots have identical reference sets and differ only in the register: one is the execution-only demonstration, the other is where a binary corpus encoder must live because rule A11 forbids a test project to name a profile assembly. ADR 0001's revision of 2026-09-07 authorises the growth.

VM-7 adds ONE composition root and it is the first image in this repository that composes two PRODUCT profiles - the end-user command-line host, taking the graph from 25 projects and 79 edges to 26 and 85. It adds ZERO packable assemblies: it is a demonstration, it declares IsPackable false, and docs/compositions.md section 1 still advertises nothing. Its reference set is the JavaScript CLI root's plus Broiler.VM.Profile.WebAssembly, so the SHAPE of the growth is one new edge kind and not one new project kind: rule N2 forbids a project in one profile family to reference a project in another and excepts a composition root, which rule A12 bounds instead, so the two families still cannot see each other and one composition can see both. Roadmap section 14 has asked since VM-3 for a catalog test over two profiles and section 16 records that a composition hosting two of them closes no gate until one exists; the only two-profile composition before this one composed two fixtures this repository wrote in order to be composed. ADR 0001's revision of 2026-09-07 authorises the growth.

VM-8 adds Broiler.VM.Profile.MachineCode, taking the graph from 26 projects and 85 edges to 27 and 88. It adds ZERO packable assemblies. It references Abstractions and Binary, providing native execution for the VM. (The edge count read 87 here until 2026-09-23 while ADR 0001's own revision of 2026-09-18 read 88 and the checkout held 88; the manifest's rows were right and this sentence was one edge short, because the same change that added the assembly also gave the slice-compiler root an edge to it and only the row was amended.)

2026-09-23 restores the arming edge to the two roots that lost it, taking the graph from 27 projects and 88 edges to 27 and 90, and adds NO project and NO packable assembly. It is a correction rather than a growth: Broiler.VM.Composition.JavaScript.Conformance and Broiler.VM.Composition.JavaScript.Cli could arm a page through Broiler.VM.Profile.JavaScript until 2026-09-18, when the arming path moved into Broiler.VM.Profile.MachineCode and was given back to Broiler.VM.Composition.JavaScript.SliceCompiler alone. For the five days between, both roots linked the encoders and not the page, so every native run they were asked for verified an artifact and then refused to instantiate it under ProfileFault/UnsatisfiedHostAssumption. The edge SHAPE is the one the slice-compiler root already has and the roots are the two the register's native-execution column now declares x86-64 for. ADR 0001's revision of 2026-09-23 records it.

UBC-1 adds Broiler.VM.Ubc, the universal bytecode ADR 0013 accepted as candidate A, taking the graph from 27 projects and 90 edges to 28 and 93: it references Broiler.VM.Abstractions and Broiler.VM.Binary and nothing else (rule U1), and the behavioural contract suite references it, because the universal bytecode's malformed corpus is replayed there. It adds ZERO packable assemblies: Broiler.VM.Ubc declares IsPackable false and carries no package identity, and whether it becomes a package is UBC-9's question.

UBC-2 adds three projects, taking the graph from 28 projects and 93 edges to 31 and 106: Broiler.VM.Emitter.Bytecode, the bytecode emitter, referencing Broiler.VM.Abstractions, Broiler.VM.Binary and Broiler.VM.Ubc; Com.Example.Tally, the universal bytecode's fixture family, an application-local consumer family referencing the same three and nothing else (rule A13 as revised); and Broiler.VM.Composition.Ubc.Fixture, the demonstration root composing the fixture family over the bytecode emitter beside Com.Example.Ledger. It adds ZERO packable assemblies: all three declare IsPackable false and carry no package identity.
